samples.question: The image shows two separate structures on a plain background. One is a dark rail drawn as a single connected stroke of constant width: it runs as three long horizontal lines joined end to end by two short vertical links, so the whole rail is one open route with exactly two loose ends and no junction. Three short bands of that rail are painted instead of dark, one orange, one purple and one yellow; each band is a piece of the rail itself. A hollow green square marker sits in clear background a short way beyond exactly one of the rail's two loose ends, and that end is the start: walking the rail from the marked end to the other end without leaving the stroke, the three coloured bands are met one after another, and that walking order is the only order that counts. The other structure is a teal wire, a separate connected staircase stroke that touches nothing else: it alternates horizontal runs with downward drops, and N is its number of downward drops, which is always 1, 2 or 3. Small gray squares are decoys and mean nothing. Consider the N-th coloured band met when walking the rail from its marked end. What colour is that band? Answer orange, purple or yellow.
